Meet the designer
“Combining creativity with thoughtful planning to shape beautiful, functional interiors that are tailored to the way people live.”

About Jane

Jane brings a project manager’s discipline to warm, livable interiors. She spent 12 years at Hyatt Regency Trinidad, including nearly five as Project Coordinator. There she worked closely with George Wong Designs on the hotel’s renovation, developing furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E) specifications and layouts, and helping make design decisions guests still experience today. She also coordinated more than 25 fit-out and furnishing projects, from pool and lobby furniture to spa and fitness upgrades.

Since 2018 she has brought that experience home, redesigning her own townhouse and a number of projects for family. Her work pairs materials, finishes and furniture to create rooms that are practical and inviting, and that are delivered on time and on budget.

Jane is currently completing SketchUp and V-Ray certification and is growing her design work into a business.

Design Approach

Every project starts with how the space is used day to day, then how it should feel.

Functionality

before decoration

Layout, storage and lighting come first, so the room works for the people who use it every day.

Balance

between comfort and style

Spaces should look good and still be easy to relax in, clean and live with.

Sustainable

and timeless

Keep what still works, refresh it where possible, and choose pieces that will not date quickly.

Featured project

Transitional Family Residence: Kitchen & Dining

TransitionalKitchenDining

A busy family kitchen with heavy honey-oak cabinetry and warm yellow walls felt dark and closed in. The goal was a lighter, calmer space that still felt warm, without the cost of new cabinets.

  • Painted the existing cabinetry a soft sage green and added brushed brass hardware
  • Kept the original countertops and backsplash, which now read as a deliberate neutral
  • Replaced the tile floor with neutral luxury vinyl planks (LVP) that mimic wood
  • Brightened the walls to white and swapped in a glass-and-brass ceiling light
  • Defined the dining area with a round walnut table, cream wingback chairs and a drum pendant
Home
1,600 sq ft
Style
Transitional
Timeline

Transitional Family Residence

Living Room, Hall & Entry

Living roomHallwayEntryway

The living spaces in the same home started with bare concrete floors and tired yellow walls. Jane carried the kitchen’s warm, light palette through the house so every room connects.

  • Laid neutral luxury vinyl planks (LVP) that mimic wood throughout
  • Painted the walls a true white
  • Brought in recessed lighting and a modern statement light in the living room
  • Furnished the living room with soft grey sofas and side tables
  • Introduced artwork to create calm interest around the spaces
  • Styled the entry with a lantern chandelier, arched mirror, console with ottomans and an olive tree
One-day makeover

A Sister’s Bedroom

BedroomSmall budget1 day

Jane’s sister did not feel comfortable in her own room, and had neither the time nor a large budget for a renovation. In a single day the room went from a crowded mix of furniture and electronics to a soft, restful retreat. Her sister fell in love with it.

  • Added picture-frame wall moulding to give the bed wall structure and focus
  • Centred the bed under a fretwork headboard, with matching white nightstands and lamps
  • Moved the TV and storage clutter out of sight
  • Layered cream bedding, a textured lumbar pillow and a blue vintage-style rug
Quick refresh

Powder Room

BathroomBudget-friendly

A small, dated powder room with yellowed walls and a heavy wood-framed mirror. Keeping the existing vanity and fixtures, a few targeted changes made it feel bright, fresh and considered.

  • Repainted the walls and trim a crisp white
  • Swapped the framed mirror for a slim black oval mirror
  • Added floating timber shelves for storage and styling
  • Installed a clear glass globe light and finished with fresh flowers
  • Replaced the old flooring with a fresh, bold black and white tile to give the small space dimension
Outdoor

Townhouse Front Garden

LandscapingLightingCurb appeal

An overgrown, patchy front bed beside the driveway. The redesign gives the entrance a clear shape and a welcoming glow after dark.

  • Cleared the bed and laid a curving lawn edged with river stone
  • Set lights into the stone border and added spotlights on the planting
  • Planted layered flowering shrubs against the wall
  • Added an oversized white bowl planter as a focal point
Outdoor living

Townhouse Patio

PatioOutdoor livingOwn home

At Jane’s own townhouse, a bare paved patio with blank concrete walls became an outdoor room for relaxing and entertaining. Press play below to see the before and after.

  • Built a feature wall of timber-look slats and vertical green panels
  • Covered the worn pavers with soft green turf
  • Furnished it with a wicker seating set and blue cushions
  • Finished with round white planters and wall lights
